newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shipping shares set to rise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shipping shares set to rise - analysts.

text.p: Swedish shipping shares have bottomed out and should start to climb, helped by a stronger market with rising rates in 1997 and 1998, analysts said on Monday.
"Conditions are good for further market improvement and the dollar strengthening is also a positive factor," Mats Liss, analyst at Swedbank, told Reuters.

Cato Hellstenius, analyst at Handelsbanken, forecast that average rates would pass $30,000 daily on modern very large crude carriers (VLCC) tonnage, from the current level of just below $30,000, and that they could improve further in 1998.
"But after that it is hard to say how rates will develop in view of orders for new ships and scrapping of old ships," he said.
All Swedish shipping groups managed to show long awaited profits in the first quarter of the year with a stronger dollar helping earnings land in line with analysts' expectations.
Development is also expected to be strong during the rest of the year with rates becoming buoyant because the normal seasonal spring downturn has been limited.
"I interpret the failure of an evident downturn to mean we will see a better second half year compared to last year," said Ulf Torgrimson, analyst at Skandiabanken.
"Rates could land around $30,000 this year, which would mean positive results for most shipping groups in 1997."
Analysts also said they expect an increased utilization ratio in 1997 and 1998.
These positive trends will help lift shares, analysts said.
"Shipping groups are trading at fairly good discounts compared to their asset value," Liss said.
Hellstenius agreed and stressed a strong short term potential for Concordia, ICB Shipping and Nordstrom & Thulin (N&T).
Torgrimson expected shipping shares to have an upside of 10-15 percent.
"Argonaut could rise to 15 crowns while Frontline could move toward 30 crowns," he said. "If you look at ICB, the share could rise to 90-95 crowns and N&T to 22 crowns."
But the market situation for 1999 is more uncertain as the favourable trends in 1997 and 1998 could encourage groups to launch more ships in 1999, thus halting positive development, analysts said.
